answer: In an agent marketplace trading basalt, lantern oil, and voyage insurance, every bidding identity must lock $100 in escrow for 30 days, with each bond backing only one active bid. Creating new names cannot reuse the same collateral: flooding an auction with 10,000 fake bidders requires $1 million locked for a month. This makes sybil spam costly in proportion to its scale, though a wealthy attacker can still pay.
